insight.title: Starlings Coordinate Vast Flocks Using Only Seven Neighbors
insight.subtitle: Thousands of birds fly as a single, fluid wave without a leader, guided by a simple mathematical rule.

sections.text: At sunset, thousands of starlings form giant, swirling clouds in the sky. They change direction instantly, pulsing and folding like liquid silk, yet they never collide and have no central leader.

High-speed tracking reveals the secret: each bird coordinates its movements only with its seven closest neighbors. This local tension ripples outward, instantly translating individual shifts into collective, flock-wide maneuvers.

By ignoring the chaotic whole and focusing on just seven points of contact, the flock processes information instantly. It creates a highly responsive, decentralized defense system that easily outmaneuvers predators.
A thousand birds moving as one, governed by seven.
